TICK_DISPATCHED: The hourly pipeline was started (GitHub accepted the dispatch).
TICK_SKIPPED: No hourly run was started: another tick started less than 50 minutes ago (LIFE-568), the same rule the workflow's gate applies.
TICK_REFUSED: GitHub refused the dispatch (401/403/404/422): the token, its permissions or the workflow name is wrong.
Replace the token (install-ticker.sh credential github) or check hourly.yml; GitHub's own crons still run meanwhile.
TICK_GITHUB_ERROR: GitHub answered the dispatch with an error (5xx or rate limit).
None; the next hour tries again and GitHub's own crons still run.
TICK_NETWORK: The Oracle machine could not reach GitHub.
None for one hour; persistent: check the VM's network.
TICKER_NO_CREDENTIAL: A stored credential (the GitHub token or the phone topic) is missing.
Run install-ticker.sh credential github / credential ntfy.
TICKER_VARIABLES_UNREADABLE: The alert switches could not be read from the repository variables, so the watchdog check did not run (it never guesses on or off).
Give the token Variables: read, or check GitHub; the GitHub watchdog still runs.
TICKER_WATCH_FAILED: The watchdog check could not read the hourly runs from GitHub.
None; the next check (15 minutes) tries again.
WATCH_DONE: The watchdog check ran (incidents opened, reminded or closed as needed).
TICKER_DRY_OK: Dry run: both credentials are present and the alert switches are readable; nothing was dispatched or pushed.
E_USAGE: The command was not `<LIFE-key> <8 hex characters>`.
Type the approval exactly as the receipt gives it.
E_NOTROOT: The runner was not started with sudo.
E_BUSY: Another pack run is in progress.
Wait for it to finish, then run again.
E_UNKNOWN_TICKET: Copy the pack folder to the host first.
E_PACK: The pack is unsafe or malformed (links, odd files, bad manifest, forbidden restore path).
Ask the agent to rebuild and republish the pack.
E_HASH: The pack's sha256 does not start with the 8 characters approved: it is not the approved pack, or it was edited.
Compare lifeos-run help with the receipt; copy the pack again.
E_TICKET: pack.json is for a different ticket than the one typed.
Use the ticket key in the receipt.
E_INTERRUPTED: The run was interrupted (Ctrl-C, SIGTERM or SIGHUP); everything declared was restored.
E_RESTORE: A step failed and the restore itself could not finish; the originals are kept in /var/lib/lifeos-runner/snapshots/.
Stop; tell the agent, who reads the result file and restores by hand with Jim.
E_RUNNER: The runner hit an unexpected error (no traceback is printed).
Tell the agent, who reads the result file.
CLOSURE_INCOMPLETE: The release closure is missing files.
ENTRY_POINT_MISSING: The release has no entry point.
NOTION_ID_INVALID: A Notion id in the release is not valid.
NOT_A_COMMIT: The release ref is not a commit.
NOT_GREEN: No hourly run has tested this commit yet.
None; the auto-release waits for a green run.
NOT_ON_MAIN: The commit is not on main.
NO_CLOSURE: The release has no closure list.
NO_NODES: No Node runtime was found on the Edge.
TREE_DIFFERS: The installed tree is not the commit's tree.
UNSAFE_CLOSURE: The closure contains an unsafe path.
READ_ONLY: The Close gate is read-only here.
None; a write was refused by design.
RESTORE_UNSAFE_PATH: A backup archive member is not a plain file or has an unsafe name, so the restore check refused to unpack it.
Do not use this archive; tell Oracle Claude.
RESTORE_TOO_BIG: The backup archive unpacks to more than the 400 MB check limit.
Tell Oracle Claude; the backup list may have grown by mistake.
RESTORE_NOTHING_UNDER_PREFIX: The restore check found no files under the requested prefix (for example hermes/).
Check that the archive is a recent nightly one and that the list includes that prefix.
RESTORE_DB_CORRUPT: A database inside the backup failed its integrity check.
Do not rely on this archive; run another backup and tell Oracle Claude.
RESTORE_DB_UNCHECKED: SQLite on this machine could not run the integrity check on a database in the backup (for example a missing extension module); this is not proof of damage.
Read the database name and SQLite message printed under the code; check it on a machine with the same extension, or on Oracle against the live copy.
RESTORE_UNREADABLE: The file is not a readable tar.gz (not decrypted yet, or damaged).
Decrypt it with the private key first, or fetch the file again.
SECRET_BAD_ARGS: The broker takes exactly one purpose name; anything extra (a secret name, URL, command or value) is refused.
Call it with the purpose name only.
SECRET_NOT_ROOT: The broker was not run as root.
SECRET_REGISTRY_UNSAFE: A purpose file is missing fields, malformed, or not root-owned and write-protected.
Fix the registry file on the host; Jim approves registry changes.
SECRET_UNKNOWN_PURPOSE: Use a registered purpose name; Jim approves a new purpose.
SECRET_CALLER_NOT_ALLOWED: The caller is not on this purpose's list.
Jim approves any change to a purpose's callers.
SECRET_RATE_LIMITED: More than 20 calls in a minute by this caller.
SECRET_AUDIT_UNAVAILABLE: The audit log could not be written, so nothing was used.
Oracle Claude checks the log path and disk.
SECRET_CRED_UNREADABLE: The encrypted host credential could not be decrypted.
Oracle Claude checks the credential file; no value is printed.
SECRET_FETCH_FAILED: The one fixed HTTPS call failed.
SECRET_BAD_REPLY: The service answered with something that is not the expected JSON, or too much.
Check the service; nothing was returned.
SECRET_FIELD_NOT_SCALAR: A listed field was not a short plain value, so nothing was returned.
SECRET_OUTPUT_TOO_LARGE: The answer exceeded 4096 bytes, so nothing was returned.
SECRET_OUTPUT_CONTAINS_SECRET: The answer would have contained the credential value in some spelling, so it was refused.
Tell Oracle Claude; the purpose must not return that field.
